title: Space Operations Specialist
raw_text:
10-40D. 40D—Space Operations Specialist (Effective 202610)
   a. Major duties. The space operations specialist serves in operating and generating force positions that
deliver space or strategic missile defense capabilities and effects to the warfighter at all levels as outlined
in JP 3-14, Space Operations, and FM 3-14, Army Space Operations in tactical and strategic multidomain
operations environments. Major duties for MOS 40D at each level of skill are:
        (1) MOSC 40D1O. Member of a space operations element, team, section, or crew that provides
space operations and strategic missile defense capabilities, products, and services. Emplaces, as
needed, and operates space operations and strategic missile defense equipment and systems,
troubleshoots issues and conducts quality control checks, and performs preventive maintenance checks
and services (PMCS) and repairs as needed. Operates and performs PMCS on assigned vehicles and
equipment. Prepares system and equipment related forms and reports. Ensures data connectivity
between operational equipment and operational Joint service networks. Initializes and operates data
networks and remote video displays. Executes offensive and defensive operations.
        (2) MOSC 40D2O. Provides technical guidance to subordinate Soldiers in the performance of their
duties. Leads small elements, teams, sections, or crews that provide space or strategic missile defense
capabilities. Trains subordinate Soldiers on space and strategic missile defense capabilities available and
provided, space operations and strategic missile defense tasks, and how to operate in a denied,
degraded, and disrupted space operational environment (D3SOE). Performs technical analysis and
provides the appropriate capability, product, service, and/or report. Provides intermediate level quality
assurance on capabilities, products, and services provided. Performs technical analysis, and ensures
appropriate action taken to initiate reports, warnings, and offensive and defensive operations.
        (3) MOSC 40D3O. Performs duties shown in the preceding skill level and provides technical
guidance to subordinate Soldiers in the performance of their duties. Leads larger space or strategic
missile defense operations elements, teams, sections, or crews. Performs liaison, operations, and training
noncommissioned officer (NCO) functions. Member of the staff in battalion and brigade level units with or
without other space operations personnel assigned where they participate in the Military Decision-Making
Process (MDMP), and advise commanders and their staff on the availability, use, and integration of space
and strategic missile defense capabilities. Coordinates with other space and strategic missile defense
operations organizations as needed. Trains staff and subordinate units on space and strategic missile
defense capabilities and how to operate in a D3SOE. Supervises emplacement, employment,
maintenance, and march order of capabilities and equipment. Organizes, participates in, and supervises
unit level space and strategic missile defense operations training and certification programs.
       (4) MOSC 40D4O. Performs duties shown in the preceding skill levels and provides technical
guidance to subordinate Soldiers in the performance of their duties. Leads space or strategic missile
defense operations sections, platoons, and detachments. Plans, organizes, supervises, and focuses the
efforts of subordinate space and strategic missile defense operations elements, teams, sections, crews,
and units and organizations, and monitors and evaluates their space and strategic missile defense related
and D3SOE training programs. Member of the staff at brigade and higher-level units with or without other
space operations personnel assigned where they participate in MDMP and effectively advise the
commander and staff on all aspects of space and strategic missile defense operations.
        (5) MOSC 40D5O. Performs all duties of preceding skill level. Supervises, plans, coordinates, and
directs the space and strategic missile defense operations provided to the warfighter at all levels in the
generating and operating force in a multidomain operations environment. Supervises, provides technical
guidance, mentors, and counsels Soldiers and NCOs. Advises the commander and staff on enlisted
personnel matters and enforces the implementation of established policies and standards. Serves as First
Sergeant in space and strategic missile defense operations companies, and as key NCO in a battalion-
level or higher staff section providing space and strategic missile defense operations-related oversight,
planning, capability development, technical advice, and assistance to commanders, staff, and subordinate
units.
        (6) MOSC 40D6O. Performs all duties of preceding skill level. Advises the commander and staff on
all matters pertaining to enlisted personnel. Enforces the implementation of established policies and
standards as they pertain to enlisted personnel within the command. Provides counsel and guidance to
 the NCOs and other enlisted Soldiers of the command. Manages the daily activities and operations of the
unit.
   b. Physical demands rating and qualification for initial award of MOS. Space Operations Specialists
must possess the following qualifications:
        (1) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
        (2) A physical profile of 222221.
        (3) Normal color vision.
        (4) Qualifying scores.
              (a) A minimum score of 110 in aptitude area EL in Army Services Vocational Aptitude Battery
(ASVAB) tests.
              (b) A minimum Occupational Physical Assessment Test (OPAT) score of Long Jump (LJ) -
0120 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic
Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles in Physical Demand Category of Moderate (Gold).
        (5) A security eligibility of Top Secret (TS) security clearance with Sensitive Compartmented
Information (SCI) access is required for initial MOS qualification training and award of the MOS.
        (6) High school graduate or equivalent prior to entry on active duty.
        (7) A U.S. citizen.
        (8) Formal training (completion of MOS 40D producing course or courses (during the period of the
interim training strategy) conducted under the auspices of the U.S. Army Space and Missile Defense
School) is mandatory unless a waiver is granted by the Office of the Chief of Space and Missile Defense.
    c. Additional skill identifiers (Note: Refer to table 12-8 for list of universal ASI’s associated with this
MOS.)
        (1) 2N – GMD Analyst (E6-E9 only) (Effective 202710)
        (2) 2P—Space Control Planner.
        (3) 2Y—Space Control Systems Operator.
        (4) D4—Sensor Leader Manager (E5-E7 only).
        (5) T3—Ground-based Midcourse Defense (GMD) System.
        (6) Y7—Sensor Manager Operations.
d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill
level are listed in the following tables:
        (1) Table 10-40D-1. Physical requirements.
        (2) Table 10-40D-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
        (3) Table 10-40D-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
